 Order

This is Third bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.870/2022 dated 17.12.2022 registered at Police Station Rampur Baghelan, District - Satna for the offences punishable under Sections 363,
366, 376, 109 of IPC and under section 3/4 of the POCSO Act and 3(2)(5) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The earlier two applications were dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 31.01.2023 passed in Smt. Varsha Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79525335/
1 M.Cr.C. No.2242/2022 and order dated 12.05.2023 passed in M.Cr.C. No.15073/2023.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.

entities.text: Smt. Varsha Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 26.12.2022 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district Satna and there is no likelihood of her absconding from the clutches of law or tamper with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

According to the prosecution, the prosecutrix who was aged more than 17 years was administered stupefying drug by the applicant and when prosecutrix went unconsciousness, she was raped by the brother of applicant.
No drug has been seized from the possession of the applicant or the place of incident.
There has been inexplicable delay of 6 days in reporting the matter.
Although there are injuries on the face of the prosecutrix, but there was no injury found in her private part.
Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court deems fit to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for her appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
